dct_description_sm: This project is based on the premise that we need to compile and synthesize existing data and information to mobilize the available knowledge base and identify gaps. The purpose is to provide an inventory of existing knowledge pertaining to regional scale coastal processes affecting the siting, planning, and management of coastal infrastructure (from the Alaska/Yukon border to Cape Dalhousie) in support of Beaufort Sea oil and gas activity. The objectives of the project are (a) to develop an inventory of existing data and research results to ensure that legacy data are exploited and accessible, (b) to provide a regional synthesis and assessment of coastal knowledge in a geo-referenced format as a basis for site selection, planning, environmental impact assessment, and regulation of coastal infrastructure including ports, and (c) in consultation with Inuvialuit and other partners, to identify new data to strengthen the regional synthesis and begin to fill any critical gaps. This ongoing activity has successfully helped to identify data gaps and will contribute to an improved knowledge of coastal processes for the Beaufort Sea region. Coastal geoscience data is the ultimate outcome of this project, which is expected to be publicly accessible by 2014.

dct_title_s: Regional Synthesis of Coastal Geoscience Data for Management of Oil and Gas Activity
